headline: What to Prepare Before Planning a Ground-Floor Home Extension
articleBody:
- [ ] Current property boundary survey — shows setback lines, easements, and buildable area.
- [ ] List of must-have room functions — defines whether you need plumbing, extra power, or specific ceiling heights.
- [ ] Existing home floor plans — helps designers understand load-bearing walls and roofline intersections.
- [ ] Drainage and utility locations — identifies underground pipes, septic lines, or meters that might need moving.
- [ ] Target overall budget with contingency — accounts for unexpected ground conditions or framing adjustments.
- [ ] HOA guidelines and restriction documents — outlines exterior aesthetic rules, roof pitches, or finish requirements.
- [ ] Insurance and licensing verification list — ensures your prospective contractor carries proper coverage and credentials.
- [ ] Temporary living and storage plan — clarifies where furniture and daily activities move during active construction.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items before inviting contractors out for estimates. Having clear boundary dimensions, functional goals, and budget boundaries organized up front prevents miscommunication and keeps project planning on track.
